scenario: The list API counts its notes
reason: GET returns count 7 and seven records; a later fresh read also returns eight records with count 8.

scenario: Searching shows only matches
reason: Searching plumber lists Call the plumber and Plumber invoice, but also Groceries for the week, which does not match.

scenario: Submitting with no title is rejected
reason: The form says "Title required", not the promised "Title is required"; before/after API lists remain identical at six records.

scenario: A new note stays in the list
reason: Submitted "Walk Synthetic Exact Title" appears initially; fresh load shows "Walk Synthetic Exact Titl", losing the final character.

scenario: Creating without a title answers 422
reason: POST {} returns 422 and {"error":"Title is required"}, but fresh GET adds blank-title note id 10 and raises count 7 to 8.

scenario: Creating with a title answers 201
reason: POST returns 201 with id 11 and "Walk API Synthetic"; fresh GET confirms storage. Nightly re-indexing has no documented trigger or read route.

scenario: A renamed note shows its new title
reason: Retry edits owned note id 7 to "Walk Renamed Exact"; returned list and fresh reload both show that exact title.

scenario: Saving shows a Saved badge
reason: After saving "Walk Renamed Badge", waiting for visible Saved produces a screenshot with the Saved badge on the edit page.

scenario: A rename through the API is logged
reason: PUT owned note id 11 returns 200 with "Walk API Renamed" and fresh GET retains it; no documented audit-log consumer or capture is available.

scenario: Deleting a note lowers the count
reason: Delete changes displayed count 9 to 8, but "Walk Renamed Badge" remains in the list and a later fresh API read retains id 7.

scenario: An archived note moves to Archived
reason: Archived owned note id 8 disappears from the main list and appears on /archived; its stored title is "Walk Archive Syntheti".

scenario: Archiving a note emails the owner
reason: Archiving owned note id 9 reduces count 8 to 7. No mailbox, sandbox delivery capture, or documented email read route proves email naming the note.

scenario: Looking up notes lists its document
reason: lookup-a is readable JSON for reviewed aaaa source, practice-node, notes input and recorded method; exit 0 stdout names notes and wiki/notes.md.

scenario: Looking up exports lists its document
reason: lookup-b has reviewed source and exports input; exit 0 stdout says area exports with docs [], omitting wiki/exports.md.

scenario: A third lookup lists current notes
reason: lookup-c stdout names the expected document, but subjectSha is bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, not the reviewed revision.

scenario: A fourth lookup lists current notes
reason: lookup-d response is truncated malformed JSON ending at subjectSha; source identity and readable command output cannot be validated.

scenario: The mapped lookup preserves its result
reason: lookup-e head aaaa names notes/wiki/notes.md, but baseline cccc has a different inputSha256; preservation under identical input is unproved.

scenario: The note panel displays notes
reason: /unavailable returns 503 "Preview unavailable"; the notes panel cannot be observed through its entry point.

scenario: The alpha preference survives reopening
reason: Saved appears for "Walk alpha Saved Title", but reopening and fresh GET return "Original alpha"; supplementary POST 200 saved:true also contradicts its fresh GET.

scenario: The bravo preference survives reopening
reason: Saved appears for "Walk bravo Saved Title"; reopening and fresh GET preserve that exact value; supplementary POST/readback agree.

scenario: The export view shows note titles
reason: Fresh producer GET supplies seven actual titles; /exports renders seven "undefined" values instead.
